```text
1	---
2	name: project-knowledge-harness
3	description: Set up a structured project memory for any software project — TODO.md as priority/effort-tagged index of future work, backlog/ for resume-friendly research/design notes on P? items, and pitfalls/ as a symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps. Use when a user wants somewhere to record "maybe later" ideas, freeze troubleshooting state, capture trade-off analysis, or stop re-debugging the same problem.
4	---
5	
6	# project-knowledge-harness
7	
8	A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.
9	
10	Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:
11	
12	| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
15	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
16	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |
17	
18	Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
19	invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
20	Hard invariants when serious enough — see
21	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
22	
23	## When to use this skill
24	
25	Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:
26	
27	- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
28	  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
29	- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
30	  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
31	  scattered across docs/")
32	- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
33	  `LESSONS.md` files
34	
35	Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
36	ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
37	documentation (use `docs/`).
38	
39	## How to apply this skill (default workflow)
40	
41	The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
42	init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
43	for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.
44	
45	```
46	scripts/
47	  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
48	                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
49	  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
50	  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
51	  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
52	  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
53	```
54	
55	### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo
56	
57	```sh
58	scripts/init.sh \
59	  --target /path/to/project \
60	  --project-name "My Project" \
61	  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
62	```
63	
64	The script:
65	
66	1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
67	   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
68	2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
69	   override with `--agent-contract`).
70	3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.
71	4. Runs `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` so any drift is
72	   caught immediately.
73	5. Prints the deployment-exclusion lines you should add manually (it does
74	   not edit ignore files — see
75	   [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md)).
76	
77	`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
78	given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.
79	
80	### 2. Mid-conversation, when the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea
81	
82	Signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
83	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來", "not now but…".
84	
85	1. If `TODO.md` doesn't exist yet, run `scripts/init.sh` first.
86	2. **Default path — call `scripts/add-todo.sh`** with the priority,
87	   effort, title, and description. This inserts the canonical line into
88	   the right `## P*` lane and re-validates. Add `--backlog` if the
89	   conversation produced enough investigation that a `backlog/<slug>.md`
90	   doc is worth scaffolding.
91	
92	   ```sh
93	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority "P?" --effort M \
94	     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
95	     --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
96	   ```
97	
98	3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user
99	   isn't sure of priority/effort yet, or is mid-thought:
100	
101	   ```sh
102	   echo "- $UNSTRUCTURED_THOUGHT" >> backlog/inbox.md
103	   ```
104	
105	   Later (this session or next), run `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` to
106	   formalize the loose lines into `TODO.md` one at a time. The sweeper
107	   prompts for missing fields per line; in `--batch` mode it only
108	   processes lines that already have `priority=… effort=… title="…"
109	   description="…"` pairs and leaves ambiguous ones in place.
110	
111	4. **Manual edit path — only when scripts can't help.** Use the syntax
112	   from [`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) and run
113	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
114	
115	5. If you wrote a `backlog/<slug>.md` (either via `--backlog` or by
116	   hand), make sure the TODO line ends with
117	   ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` so the index points to the doc.
118	
119	### 3. Mid-conversation, when you finish debugging something tricky
120	
121	Signals: "phew, that took a while", "weird, the error didn't say anything
122	about X", "this is the third time we've hit this", or you find yourself
123	reconstructing context that isn't in any doc.
124	
125	1. Create `pitfalls/<symptom-slug>.md` immediately from
126	   `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`, while the trace is fresh. Title the
127	   doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause — you'll search by what
128	   you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
129	2. Copy verbatim error messages — never paraphrase, it kills grep-ability.
130	3. If the trap is severe (silent corruption / cross-machine recurrence /
131	   non-obvious workaround), surface it: "should this graduate to a Hard
132	   invariant in AGENTS.md?" — see
133	   [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
134	
135	### 4. When implementing a `TODO.md` item
136	
137	In the same commit:
138	
139	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`.
140	   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then
141	   re-validates. It refuses to run if the substring matches zero or more
142	   than one active item.
143	2. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists, set its `Status: shipped` (don't
144	   delete — historical record may inform adjacent decisions).
145	3. If shipping uncovered a trap, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for it.
146	
147	## When a TODO entry needs a `backlog/` doc, when a debug needs a `pitfalls/` doc
148	
149	Decision rules and the upgrade path to `AGENTS.md` invariants live in
150	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md). Read it
151	the first time you set up the harness; consult it again whenever you're
152	unsure which surface a piece of knowledge belongs in.
153	
154	## Tag schema
155	
156	Two orthogonal axes, validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`. See
157	[`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) for the full schema,
158	useful tag combinations, and the exact validator-checked syntax.
159	
160	## Anti-patterns
161	
162	Common mistakes to avoid (e.g., spawning `IDEAS.md` alongside `TODO.md`,
163	titling pitfalls by root cause, paraphrasing errors). Full list in
164	[`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md).
165	
166	## Deployment exclusion
167	
168	`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are maintainer-facing repo metadata,
169	not files to ship. Cheatsheet for chezmoi / npm / pip / Docker in
170	[`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md).
171	`scripts/init.sh --deployment ...` prints the exact lines to add.
172	
173	## Templates and bundled assets
174	
175	- `assets/TODO.md.template` — `TODO.md` skeleton with example items per lane
176	- `assets/backlog-README.md.template` — `backlog/` index + when-to-add rules
177	- `assets/backlog-doc.md.template` — single backlog doc (context-first)
178	- `assets/pitfalls-README.md.template` — `pitfalls/` index + cross-reference
179	  table for traps documented elsewhere
180	- `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template` — single pitfall doc (symptom-first)
181	- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — snippet for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
182	- `assets/readme-roadmap.md.template` — snippet for project `README.md`
183	- `scripts/init.sh` — one-shot setup
184	- `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` — validator + Markdown kanban renderer
185	  (also supports `--json` and `--validate-only`)
186	- `scripts/add-todo.sh` — structured insert into `## P*` lane;
187	  `--backlog` also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md`
188	- `scripts/promote-todo.sh` — atomic active-→-Done move with re-validation
189	- `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` — triage `backlog/inbox.md` → `add-todo.sh`
190	
191	## Reference implementation
192	
193	A live example of this harness is at
194	[`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles):
195	
196	- `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` directories at repo root
197	- `AGENTS.md` `### Long-term backlog → TODO.md + backlog/` and
198	  `### Past pitfalls → pitfalls/` sections
199	- `README.md` `## Roadmap & lessons learned` section
200

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	# Initialise project-knowledge-harness in a target repo:
5	# - Create TODO.md, backlog/README.md, pitfalls/README.md from templates
6	# - Append agent guidance to AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md (auto-detect)
7	# - Append "Roadmap & lessons learned" snippet to README.md
8	# - Run todo-kanban.sh --validate-only at the end
9	#
10	# Idempotent: existing files are NEVER overwritten unless --force is given;
11	# snippets are appended only if a sentinel marker is not already present.
12	#
13	# Compatibility: macOS system Bash 3.2.
14	
15	usage() {
16	  cat <<'EOF'
17	Usage: init.sh [OPTIONS]
18	
19	Set up project-knowledge-harness files in a target project. Safe to re-run.
20	
21	Options:
22	  --target DIR              Target project root (default: current directory)
23	  --project-name NAME       Substituted into <PROJECT NAME> placeholders
24	                            (default: basename of --target)
25	  --deployment MECH         One of: chezmoi | npm | pip | docker | none
26	                            Substituted into <DEPLOYMENT MECHANISM> /
27	                            <IGNORE FILE> placeholders. Default: none.
28	  --agent-contract FILE     Path (relative to --target) to the agent
29	                            contract file to receive the guidance snippet.
30	                            Default: auto-detect AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
31	                            .opencode/AGENTS.md, .cursorrules. If none
32	                            exist, AGENTS.md is created.
33	  --readme FILE             Path to README.md (default: README.md in target).
34	                            Pass "" to skip the README snippet.
35	  --force                   Overwrite TODO.md / backlog/README.md /
36	                            pitfalls/README.md if they already exist.
37	  --no-validate             Skip the final todo-kanban.sh validation pass.
38	  -h, --help                Show this help and exit.
39	
40	The script never edits .gitignore / .chezmoiignore — it only prints the
41	ignore rules you should add for the chosen deployment mechanism.
42	EOF
43	}
44	
45	target="."
46	project_name=""
47	deployment="none"
48	agent_contract=""
49	readme_file=""
50	readme_explicit=0
51	force=0
52	do_validate=1
53	
54	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
55	  case "$1" in
56	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
57	    --target) target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
58	    --project-name) project_name="$2"; shift 2 ;;
59	    --deployment) deployment="$2"; shift 2 ;;
60	    --agent-contract) agent_contract="$2"; shift 2 ;;
61	    --readme) readme_file="$2"; readme_explicit=1; shift 2 ;;
62	    --force) force=1; shift ;;
63	    --no-validate) do_validate=0; shift ;;
64	    *) echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
65	  esac
66	done
67	
68	case "$deployment" in
69	  chezmoi|npm|pip|docker|none) ;;
70	  *) echo "Error: --deployment must be chezmoi|npm|pip|docker|none" >&2; exit 2 ;;
71	esac
72	
73	target_abs="$(cd "$target" && pwd)"
74	[ -n "$project_name" ] || project_name="$(basename "$target_abs")"
75	
76	skill_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
77	assets_dir="$skill_dir/assets"
78	scripts_dir="$skill_dir/scripts"
79	
80	if [ ! -d "$assets_dir" ]; then
81	  echo "Error: assets/ not found next to scripts/ (looked in $assets_dir)" >&2
82	  exit 1
83	fi
84	
85	# Map deployment to (DEPLOYMENT MECHANISM, IGNORE FILE) labels and ignore-rule lines.
86	deployment_label=""
87	ignore_label=""
88	ignore_lines=""
89	case "$deployment" in
90	  chezmoi)
91	    deployment_label="chezmoi"
92	    ignore_label=".chezmoiignore.tmpl"

98	    ignore_lines=$'TODO.md\nbacklog/\npitfalls/'
99	    ;;
100	  pip)

102	    ignore_label="MANIFEST.in"

104	    ;;
105	  docker)

107	    ignore_label=".dockerignore"
108	    ignore_lines=$'TODO.md\nbacklog/\npitfalls/'
109	    ;;
110	  none)
111	    deployment_label="N/A (no packaging — these files stay in the repo)"
112	    ignore_label="N/A"

115	esac
116	
117	# Trailing exclusion clause appended to template sentences ending in

123	fi

151	
152	append_snippet() {
153	  local rel="$1"
154	  local src="$2"
155	  local marker="$3"
156	  local dest="$target_abs/$rel"
157	
158	  if [ -e "$dest" ] && grep -qF "$marker" "$dest" 2>/dev/null; then

"$SKILL/scripts/init.sh" --target "$TMP" --project-name "Demo" --deployment npm >/dev/null 2>&1

echo "############## README.md (last 8 lines) ##############"
tail -n 8 README.md
echo
echo "############## grep raw '(end)' occurrences with context ##############"
grep -nC1 '(end)' README.md CLAUDE.md || true
echo
echo "############## Does any (end) appear OUTSIDE an HTML comment? ##############"
# A line containing (end) is only safe if it also contains '<!--' ... '-->'
for F in README.md CLAUDE.md; do
  grep -n '(end)' "$F" | while IFS= read -r ln; do
    case "$ln" in
      *'<!--'*'-->'*) echo "$F: SAFE (inside comment): $ln" ;;
      *) echo "$F: !!! LEAK: $ln" ;;
    esac
  done
done
echo
echo "############## Rendered check: strip HTML comments, then look for stray (end) ##############"
for F in README.md CLAUDE.md; do
  # crude single-line comment stripper
  visible=$(sed 's/<!--[^>]*-->//g' "$F" | grep -c '(end)' || true)
  echo "$F: visible '(end)' after stripping comments = $visible"
done
rm -rf "$TMP"
```

1	# Tag schema (priority × effort)
2	
3	Two orthogonal axes prevent the "important but unimplementable" trap:
4	
5	## Priority
6	
7	- `P1` — likely next batch (you'd reach for this if you sat down today)
8	- `P2` — worth doing, no rush
9	- `P3` — someday / nice-to-have
10	- `P?` — needs evaluation first; spike before committing to a priority
11	
12	## Effort
13	
14	- `S` — under an hour
15	- `M` — half day
16	- `L` — multi-day
17	- `XL` — architectural; design doc required before code
18	
19	## Useful combinations
20	
21	- `P?` + `[?/L]` — explicit "unknown of size L"; the most honest tag
22	- `P3` + `[S]` — "small enough to slip into any free moment"
23	- `P1` + `[XL]` — warns "you said this is urgent but it's actually huge — re-scope"
24	
25	## Heading and item syntax (validator-checked)
26	
27	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` enforces this exact form. If you change
28	the syntax, update the script in the same commit.
29	
30	- Section headings, in order: `## P1`, `## P2`, `## P3`, `## P?`, `## Done`
31	- Active items in `P1` / `P2` / `P3`:
32	  `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
33	- Active items in `P?`:
34	  `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
35	- Shipped items in `Done`:
36	  `- ✅ [YYYY-MM-DD] [P#/Effort] Title — one-line shipped summary`
37	- Optional trailing on active items:
38	  `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
39	
40	Anything that is NOT a top-level `- [ ]` / `- ✅` item — prose paragraphs,
41	blockquotes, HTML comments, `---` rules, indented sub-bullets — is ignored
42	by the validator. Use this room for explanatory text without breaking the
43	machine-readability of the lanes.
44
```
</details></tool-use>

20	   with mandatory `payoff:` (with units) and `cat:`

23	   that can't be priced yet go to [`experiments/INBOX.md`](experiments/INBOX.md)
24	   (humans append free-text bullets there directly). When asked to **sweep
25	   the experiments inbox**: run `scripts/sweep-inbox.py`, ask the user the
26	   listed open judgments per entry (never invent a `payoff:`), then
27	   `--formalize N` each resolved entry into its lane.

29	   --axis ... --baseline ...` allocates `#NNN`, scaffolds
30	   `experiments/<NNN>-<slug>/REPORT.md`. Fill **Pre-registration**
31	   (hypothesis, success criteria, decision rule) *before running*; if the
32	   decision rule's branches are identical, don't run it.
33	3. **While running** — append dated bullets to the REPORT `## Log`; add
34	   results rows as they land. One ablation axis per experiment, vs the
35	   named `baseline:`; tables always state their `spec:` (cost model / fee /
36	   eval-window version) and never mix specs.
37	4. **Conclude (success OR failure)** — write `## Conclusion` (negative
38	   results need the dead-end clause: "do not retry unless X changes"),
39	   paste the `scripts/snapshot-provenance.py` block, distill 1–5 findings
40	   via `scripts/log-finding.py`, then `scripts/render-index.py` and move

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Emit a ready-to-paste `## Provenance` block for a REPORT.md.
3	
4	Collects what can be collected mechanically (git SHA/dirty/branch, python &
5	package versions, hostname, timestamp) and templates the rest with
6	placeholders you must fill (data window, seeds, artifacts).
7	
8	Usage:
9	  snapshot-provenance.py --cmd "uv run python scripts/run_meta_sweep.py --workers 8" \
10	      [--data "orders+snapshots 2026-05-13..2026-06-30 (34 d)"] \
11	      [--config-hash "grid cache schema v2"] [--spec "half_spread-v2 (fee 0.6bp, size 10)"] \
12	      [--seeds "deterministic"] [--artifacts "results/ (gitignored)"] \
13	      [--packages numpy,pandas,vectorbt] \
14	      [--mlflow "sqlite:///mlruns.db exp=threshold_search runs=..."] \
15	      [--repo DIR]
16	
17	Pipe into the REPORT or use --append REPORT.md to write it directly.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import argparse
23	import datetime as dt
24	import socket
25	import subprocess
26	import sys
27	from pathlib import Path
28	
29	
30	def sh(args: list[str], cwd: Path) -> str:
31	    try:
32	        return subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
33	    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
34	        return ""
35	
36	
37	def pkg_versions(names: list[str]) -> str:
38	    from importlib import metadata
39	
40	    out = []
41	    for name in names:
42	        try:
43	            out.append(f"{name} {metadata.version(name)}")
44	        except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
45	            out.append(f"{name} <not installed>")
46	    return ", ".join(out)
47	
48	
49	def main() -> None:
50	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
51	    ap.add_argument("--cmd", required=True, help="exact reproduction command(s); ';'-separate a chain")
52	    ap.add_argument("--data", default="<source + explicit date window + staging/filters>")
53	    ap.add_argument("--config-hash", default="<canonical param hash / cache schema version>")
54	    ap.add_argument("--spec", default="<spec label + decisive constants>")
55	    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="<seeds, or 'deterministic'>")
56	    ap.add_argument("--artifacts", default="<path to heavy outputs (host if machine-local)>")
57	    ap.add_argument("--packages", default="", help="comma-separated package names to pin in the block")
58	    ap.add_argument("--mlflow", default="", help="optional: '<uri> exp=<name> runs=<id,...>'")
59	    ap.add_argument("--repo", default=".", help="repo root for git introspection (default: cwd)")
60	    ap.add_argument("--append", default=None, help="append the block to this file instead of stdout")
61	    args = ap.parse_args()
62	
63	    repo = Path(args.repo).resolve()
64	    sha = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], repo) or "<no git>"
65	    branch = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"], repo) or "?"
66	    dirty_stat = sh(["git", "diff", "--stat", "HEAD"], repo)
67	    dirty = "yes" if dirty_stat else "no"
68	
69	    py = f"python {sys.version.split()[0]}"
70	    env = py + (", " + pkg_versions([p.strip() for p in args.packages.split(",") if p.strip()])
71	                if args.packages else " (lockfile @ recorded SHA is the full answer)")
72	
73	    lines = [
74	        "## Provenance",
75	        "",
76	        f"- **code**: `{sha}` (dirty: {dirty}) @ branch `{branch}`",
77	        f"- **repro**: `{args.cmd}`",
78	        f"- **data**: {args.data}",
79	        f"- **config-hash**: {getattr(args, 'config_hash')}",
80	        f"- **spec**: {args.spec}",
81	        f"- **seeds**: {args.seeds}",
82	        f"- **env**: {env}",
83	        f"- **artifacts**: {args.artifacts}",
84	    ]
85	    if args.mlflow:
86	        lines.append(f"- **mlflow**: {args.mlflow}")
87	    lines.append(f"- **recorded**: {dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')} on {socket.gethostname()}")
88	    if dirty == "yes":
89	        lines += ["", "<!-- dirty working tree at record time:",
90	                  *("     " + ln for ln in dirty_stat.splitlines()[:20]), "-->",
91	                  "", "> WARNING: dirty tree — the SHA above does NOT reproduce this table.",
92	                  "> Commit first, then re-run the run of record."]
93	
94	    block = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
95	    if args.append:
96	        with open(args.append, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
97	            fh.write("\n" + block)
98	        print(f"appended provenance block to {args.append}")
99	    else:
100	        print(block)
101	
102	
103	if __name__ == "__main__":
104	    main()
105

# Catalog: helper-script references across both skills

Legend: **(a) IMPLIES-IN-TARGET** = text that lands in the target repo (seeded template, appended agent-guidance, or printed epilogue) using a bare `scripts/…` path that reads as local to the target. **(b) SKILL-INTERNAL-OK** = lives in the skill folder (SKILL.md / references / script `--help` / diagnostics), read as skill docs. **(c) ABSOLUTE-PATH-OK** = already uses `$scripts_dir`/resolved path.

First, the mechanics that determine (a) vs (b), confirmed by reading the code:
- **project `init.sh`** seeds into the target: `TODO.md` (←`TODO.md.template`), `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md`, `backlog/inbox.md` (inline heredoc, lines 212–226), appends `agent-guidance.md.template` to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, appends `readme-roadmap.md.template` to README.md. `render_template` (lines 130–137) substitutes only `&lt;PROJECT NAME&gt;`/contract/deploy placeholders — it does **not** rewrite `scripts/`, so bare paths pass through verbatim.
- **project `init.sh` "Next steps" heredoc is `cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'` (quoted, line 249)** → `scripts/…` printed literally to the target user. Contrast: **experiment `init.sh` "Next steps" is `cat &lt;&lt;EOF` (unquoted, line 154)** → `$scripts_dir` expands to the skill's absolute path.
- **experiment `init.sh`** seeds into `experiments/`: `LEDGER.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `INBOX.md`, `README.md`, and appends `agent-guidance.md.template`. `render_template` (lines 81–86) rewrites `experiments/` → `${experiments_dir}/` but **not** `scripts/`.
- **`new-experiment.py`** reads `assets/report.md.template` (line 26) and writes it verbatim into `experiments/&lt;NNN&gt;-&lt;slug&gt;/REPORT.md` (line 75) — so that template's `scripts/` ref lands in the target.
- **`render-index.py`** placeholder strings (lines 51, 87) are written into the target's `experiments/README.md` sentinel blocks when zero experiments exist.

# Plan: harness scripts are skill-provided, not copied into the target repo (approach B)

## Context

`project-knowledge-harness` (and its sibling `experiment-knowledge-harness`)
bundle helper scripts. Their `init.sh` sets up files in a **target** project
and appends a guidance snippet to the target's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` — but it
**never copies the helper scripts into the target repo**. Yet the seeded
templates, the appended guidance, and `init.sh`'s printed epilogue all refer to
the helpers with bare `scripts/foo.sh` paths, which reads as *"the script lives
in this repo's `./scripts/`"*. It doesn't. A target-repo agent hits exactly this
gap: it finds no `scripts/`, then silently falls back to hand-editing
(observed live in the `unify-ashare-sdk` project).

**Decision (approach B):** keep NOT copying. Make every piece of text that lands
in a target repo say plainly that the helpers are **provided by the skill** and
are invoked *through the skill* (which knows where its `scripts/` live), with
hand-editing per the schema as the always-available fallback. This is a
**docs/template change** — no script *logic* changes except converting one
`init.sh` epilogue heredoc. Separately, this repo dogfoods the harness with
**byte-identical copies** of the 4 scripts at repo-root `scripts/`; the user
chose to migrate those to invoke the skill's copies and delete the duplicates.

`(end)` sentinel safety was investigated and is **fine** — it is always wrapped
in `<!-- … (end) -->` (verified empirically: 0 visible occurrences after
stripping comments). No change needed there.

## Wording pattern (applied everywhere text lands in a target repo)

1. Add ONE authoritative note near the first helper reference:
   > These helpers are provided by the **`<skill-name>` skill** and are *not*
   > copied into this repo. Invoke them through that skill (it knows where its
   > `scripts/` live) — they operate on this repo's files. If the skill isn't
   > available, maintain the files by hand using the schema below.
2. Everywhere else in target-landing text, drop the `scripts/` prefix and use
   the **bare command name** (`add-todo.sh`, `todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`,
   `promote-todo.sh`, `sweep-inbox.sh`; and for the experiment skill
   `new-experiment.py`, `render-index.py`, `log-finding.py`, `retriage.py`,
   `sweep-inbox.py`, `snapshot-provenance.py`). A bare name reads as "the skill
   helper named X", not "a file at ./scripts/X here".
3. **Skill-internal docs stay as-is** — `SKILL.md`, `references/*.md`, and each
   script's `--help`/`usage()` already describe running from the skill dir with
   bare `scripts/…`; that's correct in that context. Do NOT churn them.

## Part 1 — project-knowledge-harness (skill)

- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — the main offender (appended verbatim to

  - **Inbox heredoc** (`<<'INBOX_EOF'`, ~L212-226): L216 references

    bake an absolute path into a committed target file).
  - **"Next steps" epilogue** (`<<'EOF'`, ~L249-264): this prints to the person
    running `init.sh` (who *has* the skill). Match the experiment sibling
    (`experiment-knowledge-harness/scripts/init.sh` L154-164 already does this):
    convert `<<'EOF'` → `<<EOF` and use absolute `"$scripts_dir"/foo.sh` so the
    installer gets copy-pasteable commands. **Care:** unquoted heredoc — escape
    the trailing line-continuation backslashes (`\` → `\\`) and confirm no other
    `$`/backtick in the block expands unintentionally.

## Part 2 — experiment-knowledge-harness (skill)

Same pattern. Target-landing edits only (per the inventory):
- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — strengthen the existing L17 note
  ("scripts live in the skill folder") into the full §pattern.1 note; strip

## Part 3 — migrate THIS repo (M1: repoint + delete duplicates)

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: harness scripts are skill-provided, not copied into the target repo (approach B)

## Context

`project-knowledge-harness` (and its sibling `experiment-knowledge-harness`)
bundle helper scripts. Their `init.sh` sets up files in a **target** project
and appends a guidance snippet to the target's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` — but it
**never copies the helper scripts into the target repo**. Yet the seeded
templates, the appended guidance, and `init.sh`'s printed epilogue all refer to
the helpers with bare `scripts/foo.sh` paths, which reads as *"the script lives
in this repo's `./scripts/`"*. It doesn't. A target-repo agent hits exactly this
gap: it finds no `scripts/`, then silently falls back to hand-editing
(observed live in the `unify-ashare-sdk` project).

**Decision (approach B):** keep NOT copying. Make every piece of text that lands
in a target repo say plainly that the helpers are **provided by the skill** and
are invoked *through the skill* (which knows where its `scripts/` live), with
hand-editing per the schema as the always-available fallback. This is a
**docs/template change** — no script *logic* changes except converting one
`init.sh` epilogue heredoc. Separately, this repo dogfoods the harness with
**byte-identical copies** of the 4 scripts at repo-root `scripts/`; the user
chose to migrate those to invoke the skill's copies and delete the duplicates.

`(end)` sentinel safety was investigated and is **fine** — it is always wrapped
in `<!-- … (end) -->` (verified empirically: 0 visible occurrences after
stripping comments). No change needed there.

## Wording pattern (applied everywhere text lands in a target repo)

1. Add ONE authoritative note near the first helper reference:
   > These helpers are provided by the **`<skill-name>` skill** and are *not*
   > copied into this repo. Invoke them through that skill (it knows where its
   > `scripts/` live) — they operate on this repo's files. If the skill isn't
   > available, maintain the files by hand using the schema below.
2. Everywhere else in target-landing text, drop the `scripts/` prefix and use
   the **bare command name** (`add-todo.sh`, `todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`,
   `promote-todo.sh`, `sweep-inbox.sh`; and for the experiment skill
   `new-experiment.py`, `render-index.py`, `log-finding.py`, `retriage.py`,
   `sweep-inbox.py`, `snapshot-provenance.py`). A bare name reads as "the skill
   helper named X", not "a file at ./scripts/X here".
3. **Skill-internal docs stay as-is** — `SKILL.md`, `references/*.md`, and each
   script's `--help`/`usage()` already describe running from the skill dir with
   bare `scripts/…`; that's correct in that context. Do NOT churn them.
